title: Fire Emblem's Nintendo 64 Game Was Cancelled and Restarted on GBA
hook: Nintendo confirmed in September 2000 that Fire Emblem 64 was dead, so Intelligent Systems started over on the Game Boy Advance and shipped The Binding Blade in 2002. Which cancelled game would you bring back? Gameplay is from Shards of Irsa, a game I'm making.
script: Did you know Fire Emblem once had a Nintendo 64 game that was cancelled before it ever came out? In the late nineties, Nintendo was building a new Fire Emblem for the 64DD, the disk drive add on for the Nintendo 64. Fans simply called it Fire Emblem 64. It later picked up a real title, Ankoku no Miko, which translates to Maiden of Darkness. But the 64DD flopped in Japan, and Intelligent Systems was going through big structural changes at the same time. In September of 2000, Nintendo confirmed that Fire Emblem 64 in its current form had stopped development. The project was put on hold earlier that year and then moved to the Game Boy Advance. The team did not port the old game over. Nintendo's own making of book says the planning basically had to start again from scratch. That restarted project became Fire Emblem: The Binding Blade, released in Japan in March of 2002. Its hero was a young lord named Roy, who had already debuted in Super Smash Bros. Melee a few months earlier. The Binding Blade never left Japan, so Western players met Roy in Smash with no idea where he came from. Which cancelled game would you bring back if you could? Follow for more gaming history.
